title: Integer division
explanation: Both operands are ints, so `/` truncates: 9/4 = 2. The remainder 9%4 = 1. 2 + 1 = 3.

title: Short-circuit order
prompt: `arr` has length 3. Which condition is safe when `i` might be 5?
options: `arr[i] > 0 && i < arr.length` — same thing, order doesn't matter
explanation: `&&` evaluates left to right and stops at the first false. Checking `i < arr.length` first means `arr[i]` is never touched when `i` is out of bounds. The reversed order throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

title: Math toolbox
code:
int bigger = Math.{{1}}(a, b);          // larger of the two
int distance = Math.{{2}}(a - b);       // always non-negative
int pow = (int) Math.{{3}}(2, 10);      // 1024 — note the cast
explanation: `Math.pow` returns `double` even for whole numbers, hence the `(int)` cast.

title: Sum of digits
prompt: Return the sum of the digits of `n` (n ≥ 0). Peel digits with `% 10` and `/ 10` in a loop: while `n > 0`, add `n % 10` to a running total, then set `n = n / 10`.

solution.explanation: `n % 10` reads the last digit; `n /= 10` removes it. The loop ends when every digit is consumed.

title: Drill: clamp
prompt: From memory: return `x` clamped into the range `[lo, hi]` — if `x < lo` return `lo`, if `x > hi` return `hi`, else `x`. One line with `Math.max` and `Math.min` is the idiomatic answer.

solution.explanation: `Math.min(x, hi)` caps the top; `Math.max(lo, ...)` lifts the bottom.

hints: Cap the top first: `Math.min(x, hi)` — then lift the result with `Math.max(lo, ...)`.

title: Recall: Math toolbox
prompt: Fill in the three Math calls you'll use constantly.
code:
int hi = Math.{{1}}(a, b);   // larger of the two
int lo = Math.{{2}}(a, b);   // smaller of the two
int d  = Math.{{3}}(a - b);  // non-negative distance
explanation: `Math.max`, `Math.min`, and `Math.abs` — the three you reach for in almost every problem.

title: Drill: range of three
prompt: From memory: return the range (largest minus smallest) of three ints, using nested `Math.max` / `Math.min`.
hints: Nest to get the max of three: `Math.max(a, Math.max(b, c))`.
Do the same with `Math.min`, then subtract.
